boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UC Davis traditions, including active campus rituals and clearly labeled historical practices from the university archives.

cards.title: Pajamarino
cards.subtitle: UC Davis homecoming pajama rally
cards.notes: Look for the current homecoming schedule if you want to attend; this pajama-clad rally traces its documented roots to 1912 and continues today.
cards.short_summary: A continuing UC Davis pajama-rally tradition with more than a century of history.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library states that present-day Pajamarino traces its roots to 1912 and that the tradition continues today.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: Check UC Davis homecoming communications for the current route, time, and participation details.

cards.title: Touch Bookhead Before Finals
cards.subtitle: Outside Peter J. Shields Library
cards.notes: Stop by the Bookhead sculpture before finals and take part in the campus good-luck ritual; treat the outcome as lore, not a guarantee.
cards.short_summary: Students touch the library-side Egghead as a finals-week good-luck custom.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library says that during finals week, students touch the Bookhead sculpture in front of Shields Library for good luck.
cards.access_notes: Bookhead is outside Peter J. Shields Library; keep clear of entrances and other visitors.

cards.title: Picnic Day
cards.subtitle: Annual UC Davis open house
cards.notes: Plan around the published April schedule and choose a parade, exhibit, or student-organization activity; the university lists the 2026 event as free.
cards.short_summary: UC Davis’ large student-run open house combines academic exhibits, a parade, and campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis lists Picnic Day for April 18, 2026, describes it as a student-run open house, and says everyone is welcome to attend the free event.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists 8 a.m.–5 p.m. on Saturday, April 18, 2026; consult its schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Whole Earth Festival
cards.subtitle: ASUCD festival on the UC Davis Quad
cards.notes: Use the festival program to pick a workshop or performance; the organizer describes this as a free, student-run, family-friendly, zero-waste event.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding student-run festival centered on art, activism, wellness, and environmental sustainability.
cards.evidence_claim: ASUCD says Whole Earth Festival began as a UC Davis art-class project, evolved into a free student-run event, and is family-friendly.
cards.access_notes: Historically held on the UC Davis Quad; confirm the current program and access information before attending.

cards.title: Little I
cards.subtitle: Student grooming and showmanship tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the Young Cattleman’s Association’s event information and observe the student showmanship tradition with the university herds.
cards.short_summary: A UC Davis livestock-show tradition begun by the Golden Hoof Club in 1937.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library records that Little I began in 1937 for student grooming and showmanship and says it is still held on campus.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: The archive identifies the UCD Young Cattleman’s Association as the current sponsor; check its current event details.

cards.title: Frosh Dinks
cards.subtitle: Historical freshman unity caps
cards.notes: View the archive photographs as a window into former campus life: freshmen wore blue-and-gold “Cal Aggie” caps, a practice that ended in the 1960s.
cards.short_summary: A discontinued freshman-cap tradition linked to an early class-rivalry contest.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library documents that freshmen wore blue dinks with a gold button and “Cal Aggie” lettering; it says the practice went out of fashion in the 1960s.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; view the archival images rather than attempting to recreate the associated class-rivalry rules.

cards.title: The President’s Reception
cards.subtitle: Historical fall welcome event
cards.notes: Explore the archive’s dated photographs and event description; this was a fall welcome reception during the 1950s and 1960s, not a current program.
cards.short_summary: A former UC president’s fall visit that welcomed new and returning Davis students.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library says that in the 1950s and 1960s the UC president visited Davis each fall for a student welcome reception.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: Historical only; the archive identifies past venues including the Memorial Union, Freeborn Hall, and Everson Hall.

cards.title: Leap-Year Labor Day
cards.subtitle: Historical campus-improvement workday
cards.notes: Read the archive account and photographs for the unusual leap-year workday, whose projects ranged from plantings to campus repairs; it ended in 1964.
cards.short_summary: A discontinued volunteer workday that eventually occurred on February 29.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library documents a student-initiated 1915 campus-improvement workday that became a leap-year activity; the last traditional event was held in 1964.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; do not undertake facilities work outside authorized UC Davis volunteer programs.

cards.title: Spring Sing
cards.subtitle: Historical living-group singing competition
cards.notes: Use the university archive’s image and caption to see how campus living groups once competed in song; the exhibit presents it as a historical event.
cards.short_summary: A former competitive-singing event involving UC Davis campus living groups.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library describes Spring Sing as a popular campus event in which all campus living groups took part in competitive singing.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: Historical exhibit entry; no current recurrence is asserted by the cited source.

cards.title: The Picnic Day Aquacade
cards.subtitle: Historical poolside Picnic Day program
cards.notes: Treat this as an archival side chapter of Picnic Day: the Aquacade combined synchronized swimming, live music, and a poolside variety show through the early 1990s.
cards.short_summary: A discontinued Picnic Day poolside variety program documented by the UC Davis archives.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Davis Library states that Picnic Day featured an Aquacade from 1948 until the early 1990s, with synchronized swimming, live music, and a poolside variety show.
cards.source_title: UC Davis Traditions: Past and Present
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; consult the current Picnic Day schedule for present-day programming.
